steps.question: Which of the ~12,000 genes differ in expression between the 6 treated and the 6 control human muscle samples, on the delivered log2(TPM+1) scale?

grounding.reason: Log-normalized input (log2(TPM+1), no counts) selects limma-trend and forbids count models per R-0019@251d; robust eBayes per R-0093@4fa4; abundance filter per R-0075@4d16; no renormalization plus range check per R-0074@06b0; explicit reference level per R-0036@9786; BH via topTable and TREAT for any LFC threshold per R-0044@1777 and R-0037@e6d8.

steps.description: Filter low-abundance genes using a mean-log-expression floor chosen from the low end of the overall expression distribution, requiring a gene to exceed the floor in at least the smallest group size (6) samples; the filter must be derived independently of the condition labels. Verify the value range is consistent with a log2 scale (roughly 0-20, fractional values) and record it — if the range instead looks like integer counts, stop and report that, because the whole method choice depends on this. Do not renormalize. Build the design ~condition with the control level set explicitly as the reference via relevel(), fit lmFit, then eBayes(trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE). Extract results with topTable(coef = treated-vs-control, adjust.method='BH', number=Inf). Additionally run treat()/topTreat() against a stated log2FC threshold (state the threshold, e.g. 1.0) so any effect-size claim is tested inside the model. Write out the full gene-level result table (logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, B) for every tested gene — this table is the input to the enrichment step, so it must not be thresholded. Produce a volcano plot and an MA-style plot, and a heatmap of the top significant genes.

eBayes is called with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE, and both are reported in the methods text

The number of genes with adj.P.Val < 0.05 is reported, alongside the number passing the TREAT test at the stated log2FC threshold; if zero genes are significant, that is reported plainly rather than the threshold being relaxed

steps.description: Take the complete unthresholded limma result table from T1S2. plan.title: Treated vs control muscle DE (limma-trend) + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12,000 x 12 matrix of log2(TPM+1) values delivered by the core facility (/data/inputs/expression/log_expr.csv) with a 12 x 2 sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv) giving 6 treated vs 6 control human muscle samples, unpaired, single batch. Because the values are already normalized log2 abundances rather than raw counts, the negative-binomial path (DESeq2, edgeR, voom) does not apply: those models require integer counts and the data profile is explicit that no counts were delivered. The plan therefore uses limma on the log values with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE empirical Bayes moderation, which models the mean-variance trend of log abundance data directly and protects against hypervariable genes at n=6 per group. T1S1 establishes sample structure (PCA/MDS on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, per-sample detection and distribution) so any outlier or unexpected grouping is named before the model rather than after. T1S2 applies an expression-independent low-abundance filter, verifies the value range is log2-consistent (no second normalization), fits ~condition with control set explicitly as the reference level, and reports the treated-vs-control contrast with BH adjustment plus a TREAT test against a stated log2FC threshold so that any effect-size claim is tested inside the model rather than filtered post-hoc. T2S1 takes the full ranked list of every tested gene into fgsea against the human MSigDB hallmark collection, with camera on the same limma fit as the correlation-aware competitive companion; the ranking statistic is a disputed choice and this plan states its side: the limma moderated t statistic (the direct analogue of the DESeq2 Wald statistic — signed and scaled by the standard error), since no Wald statistic exists on this path. T1S3 assembles the report with the reproducibility record. The design is small (n=6 per arm) and single-batch, so the analysis is adequately powered only for moderate-to-large effects; the report must state this rather than imply otherwise.

Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seed, package and collection versions; leading-edge genes per significant set
Sample structure QC on log abundance values: MDS or PCA, sample distances, detected genes
Low abundance filter on TPM, FPKM, or log expression values

steps.name: Consolidated report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control muscle', with the method, thresholds, counts and limitations stated so a reader can reproduce and judge it?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2 and T2S1. State: the method (limma-trend on core-facility log2(TPM+1) values, with the explicit reason a count model was not used); every package version; the design formula, the reference level and the named contrast; the abundance floor and the FDR and log2FC thresholds; the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000; the number of differentially expressed genes at the stated FDR and the number passing TREAT. Present the ranked gene table, the volcano, and the top-gene heatmap. For enrichment, state the gene set database and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the tool and version, and the multiple-testing method; list the leading-edge genes per significant set; state explicitly that enrichment results are method-dependent and are hypotheses for follow-up. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seed, package versions, gene set collection version, and the annotation package release. State the power limitation of n=6 per group directly, and state plainly if the number of significant genes is small or zero rather than reframing it.
steps.context: Final synthesis step for the 6 treated vs 6 control human muscle log2(TPM+1) analysis. No new statistics are computed here.
acceptance_criteria: Method, package versions, design formula, reference level, named contrast, and all thresholds are stated
Number of genes tested after filtering (out of 12,000) and number of DE genes per criterion are stated
The reason a count-based model was not used (log2(TPM+1) input, no counts delivered) is stated explicitly in the methods
Enrichment reporting includes database, version, rank metric, universe, size window, tool version, and multiple-testing method
Leading-edge genes are listed per significant gene set
A method-dependence caveat for the enrichment result is included
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seed, package versions, collection version and annotation release is stored with the results
The n=6-per-group power limitation is stated, and a null or weak result is reported as such
constraints: Report every field listed in the constraints of the source steps; do not omit the counts of tested and significant genes
Do not restate an exploratory signal as a conclusion
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
caveats: This is a single-cohort, single-batch, n=6-per-group study; no external validation cohort is part of this analysis, so every finding is internal and unreplicated
